title: sdk(python): add connect/read/overall timeout model and map to httpx
author: Sabrina James
description: Context: As part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative, we need a single timeout model that behaves predictably across Python/TS/Go and can be mapped cleanly onto each language's underlying HTTP client. We also have multiple support reports (notably SUP-29410) that Python streaming appears to ignore configured timeouts, plus internal feedback that timeouts are hard to reason about because we currently treat a single float as "some" timeout without clarifying whether it is connect vs read vs overall. What this PR does: Implements the v1 timeout model for the Python SDK with explicit connect/read/overall semantics, and maps those to httpx.Timeout consistently for both streaming and non-streaming requests. Adds migration notes and tests to lock behavior and prevent regression. Behavior / API changes: 1) Adds a new Timeouts type (redwood.timeouts.Timeouts) with fields connect_s, read_s, overall_s. The SDK accepts this via Client(timeouts=Timeouts(...)) and request overrides (e.g. client.chat.completions.create(..., timeouts=...)). 2) Maintains backwards compatibility for Client(timeout=...) but deprecates it (warning) and defines a stable mapping: timeout=<float> is treated as overall_s. connect_s/read_s use defaults unless explicitly set. 3) Streaming: read timeout is still honored for idle reads (i.e., if the stream stalls and no bytes are received within read_s, we raise RedwoodTimeoutError). overall_s caps total request wall time including streaming. 4) Request cancellation via context manager / generator close now reliably aborts the underlying httpx request and stops background reads (important for avoiding hung sockets). Defaults (aligned with ADR-sdk-timeout-model): connect_s=10, read_s=60, overall_s=300. Note: these are intentionally conservative for non-streaming; streaming callers are expected to set read_s higher if they expect long gaps between events (docs follow-up in ENG-5128). Error typing: Introduces RedwoodTimeoutError (subclass of RedwoodAPIError) surfaced consistently with request_id when available. Implementation notes: - Centralized timeout resolution in _client.py so precedence is: per-request override > Client.timeouts > deprecated Client.timeout > env var REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_S (deprecated) > default. - Uses httpx.Timeout(connect=..., read=..., write=..., pool=...) with write/pool derived from connect_s unless explicitly overridden internally; overall_s is implemented via httpx's "timeout" plus an explicit wall-clock deadline enforced in our request wrapper to avoid edge cases where streaming iterators can outlive a request timeout. - Adds a small helper (timeouts.py) that clamps/validates values (non-negative, overall >= max(connect, read) if all present), and normalizes ints/floats. Tests: - Unit tests for resolution/precedence (client vs request override, env var fallback, deprecated alias mapping). - Integration-ish tests with MockTransport to simulate: connect timeout, read stall on streaming, overall deadline exceeded mid-stream. - Golden assertions for exception shape (type, message, retryable=false, request_id present when response headers include x-request-id). Migration notes included below and in docstrings. Migration notes (tl;dr): Existing code using Client(timeout=30) still works, but will emit a DeprecationWarning; update to Client(timeouts=Timeouts(overall_s=30)) or set granular values. If you were relying on the old behavior where streaming could run indefinitely despite timeout configuration, you may now see RedwoodTimeoutError unless you increase read_s/overall_s for streaming workloads.
commits: sdk: add Timeouts model + validation helpers
sdk: implement timeout precedence + httpx mapping
sdk: enforce overall deadline for streaming iterators
tests: add timeout resolution + streaming stall coverage
docsstrings: add migration notes and examples
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can we make sure the precedence order matches the draft standard? Specifically per-request > client > env > default, and the deprecated alias shouldn't override explicit granular values. Also please confirm what we do if overall < read. Sabrina James (author): Updated resolve_timeouts() to follow per-request > Client.timeouts > deprecated Client.timeout > env var > default. Added validation: if overall_s is set and (connect_s/read_s) are set, we raise ValueError when overall_s < max(connect_s, read_s) to avoid silent surprises. For backward compat when only overall_s is set, we keep defaults for connect/read. Allison Grant: Please avoid writing our own timer loops if httpx already enforces total timeout; timer loops can be flaky under event loop scheduling. Also, we need the error shape to include timeout_ms and request_id where possible for parity with ENG-5129. Sabrina James (author): Agreed. We still use httpx.Timeout for connect/read/pool/write. The extra overall deadline enforcement is only applied around streaming iteration because we saw cases where the initial response was within timeout but iteration could run indefinitely; the wrapper enforces a wall-clock deadline and cancels the response stream on expiry. Added fields on RedwoodTimeoutError: timeout_ms and phase (connect/read/overall). Request_id is pulled from headers when available (x-request-id) and from JSON error bodies when present. Owen Phillips: The SUP-29410 repro was "timeout not honored on streaming". Can we add a regression test that simulates a stream that emits one chunk then stalls, and assert we error out with a typed exception that includes request_id? Sabrina James (author): Added tests/test_streaming_timeouts.py::test_stream_read_timeout_on_stall and ::test_stream_overall_timeout_mid_stream. Both use MockTransport and a fake byte iterator; we attach x-request-id and assert it propagates into RedwoodTimeoutError. Ibrahim Khan: One more: DeprecationWarning should be quiet by default in normal runs; but we should document it and add a single warning on client init, not per-request. Sabrina James (author): Updated to warn once on Client construction when timeout= is passed. No per-request warnings. Ibrahim approved. Allison approved after confirming error fields and defaults. Owen approved after verifying SUP repro passes locally.

release_notes: Python SDK: Added Timeouts(connect_s, read_s, overall_s) and standardized timeout behavior across streaming and non-streaming requests.
Client(timeout=...) remains supported but is deprecated; use Client(timeouts=Timeouts(...)) instead.
Streaming now honors read and overall timeouts consistently; stalled streams will raise RedwoodTimeoutError with request_id when available.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main; included in upcoming python SDK parity release train (see ENG-5123).
